items.lp_book_number: Worked example: Lali and the rising Sun
items.question_text: Lali faces the rising Sun on the school ground. She then turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. Which direction is she facing now, and which direction is behind her?
items.reason: The question names no picture and gives everything in words (east is where the Sun rises, turn to the left hand). A top-down picture of Lali with a compass would only make it nicer; not added. Figure that would help: Lali seen from above facing the rising Sun with her left hand marked north.
items.text_alternative: Keep as text: facing east, the left hand points north.

diagram.manim_description: On a 16 x 9 unit white canvas (1 unit = 120 px) draw a top-down view of a boy who faces the Sun, with no compass. Draw the boy's stretched arms first: a vertical INK line 5 px wide from (6.0, 2.2) to (6.0, 6.8), with a small circle of radius 0.22 filled CELL_FILL and outlined INK at each end (the hands). On top of the line draw his head: a circle of radius 0.55 centred at (6.0, 4.5), filled CELL_FILL, outline INK 3 px. Draw his nose as a small solid INK triangle with vertices (6.55, 4.2), (6.55, 4.8) and (6.95, 4.5), so the boy looks to the right. From (7.3, 4.5) to (11.4, 4.5) draw a dashed GUIDE arrow 3 px wide with its arrow-head at the right end. At (12.6, 4.5) draw the Sun: a circle of radius 0.8 filled #F6D55C with a #E0A800 outline and 12 equally spaced short rays of length 0.35 starting 0.15 outside the circle. Write 'Rising Sun' in INK below the Sun, centred at (12.6, 5.85). Draw nothing else: no compass, no direction letters, no arrows labelled with directions, no other children.
must_not_show: any direction word (North, East, South, West) or letter N, E, S, W
accuracy_checks: the boy's nose points right, towards the Sun, and the dashed arrow runs from the nose to the Sun (7.3 to 11.4 on y = 4.5)
the arms line is perpendicular to the facing direction (vertical line, boy faces right)
no direction word or compass letter appears, so the figure does not give away where west is

items.reason: The question is about a playground picture with a compass: a 2 x 2 arrangement read with the compass. The learner reads directions off that picture, so the picture is the figure the example needs. Borderline: the layout is also stated in words.
